1. Core Clinical Tension: A 71-year-old diabetic male with previous stroke presents with warm, erythematous, fluctuant, and painful right ankle swelling that has progressed indolently for over a month without trauma or systemic constitutional symptoms (afebrile, no cough, no night sweats). Ankle imaging demonstrates a complex abscessed tenosynovitis with soft-tissue gas tracking between bone structures, accompanied by markedly elevated CRP (138.7 mg/L) and hyperfibrinogenemia. The presence of soft tissue gas and an acute inflammatory appearance in a diabetic host creates profound clinical tension between classic pyogenic or gas-forming bacterial necrotizing tenosynovitis/arthritis and an indolent, paucisymptomatic mycobacterial infection.

2. Admission Breakpoint: Evaluation terminates after physical examination, triage blood tests (normochromic microcytic anemia, lymphopenia, elevated CRP, elevated fibrinogen, normal renal/liver function, negative viral serology), soft-tissue ankle ultrasound, and ankle CT scan (showing soft tissue gas and diffuse infiltration), strictly prior to surgical joint lavage, routine aerobic/anaerobic bacteriological cultures, mycobacterial stains/cultures, and chest CT.

3. Differential Distinctions: Acute pyogenic or gas-producing bacterial septic arthritis/tenosynovitis is ruled out by persistent sterility of aerobic and anaerobic cultures over 15 days and lack of improvement on empirical management. Diabetic neuroarthropathy (Charcot joint) is excluded by frank abscess fluid and positive mycobacterial testing. Targeted AFB microscopy, MGIT/Lowenstein-Jensen cultures, and GeneXpert PCR definitively confirm osteoarticular tuberculosis.
case_prompt:
A 71-year-old male with a medical history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, essential hypertension, and stable right hemiparesis secondary to a prior ischemic stroke presented to the hospital with swelling of his right ankle that had been progressively worsening over the preceding month. He reported no preceding mechanical trauma or falls. Systemic review was negative for fever, fatigue, chills, night sweats, cough, dysuria, or diarrhea, and he had no documented personal or household exposure to chronic granulomatous illnesses.

On physical examination, the patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Blood pressure was 120/50 mmHg, heart rate was 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate was 18 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation was 94% on ambient air. Right ankle examination revealed warm, erythematous, fluctuant, and tender swelling over the joint. Active and passive mobilization of the ankle elicited severe pain. Neurological examination showed baseline right-sided motor deficit with preserved orientation (Glasgow Coma Scale 15/15). Pulmonary auscultation demonstrated clear breath sounds bilaterally without adventitious sounds, and cardiovascular examination was normal.

Baseline laboratory investigations revealed normochromic microcytic anemia with a hemoglobin of 9.5 g/dL and absolute lymphopenia of 0.5 × 10⁹/L, while total leukocyte and platelet counts were within reference ranges. Coagulation profiling showed an elevated fibrinogen level of 9.1 g/L, an activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) ratio of 1.6, and a prothrombin time (PT) of 61%. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP) was markedly elevated at 138.7 mg/L. Serum electrolytes, renal function (urea 0.25 g/L, creatinine 6 mg/L), and liver function tests (AST 8 IU/L, ALT 12 IU/L) were all normal. Serologic assays for HIV, hepatitis B virus, and hepatitis C virus were negative.

Bedside soft-tissue ultrasonography of the right ankle demonstrated a poorly circumscribed, hypoechoic, heterogeneous fluid collection extending into the joint cavity with infiltration of adjacent muscular and tendinous structures, suggestive of abscessed tenosynovitis and myositis. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the right ankle revealed diffuse soft-tissue infiltration with significant gas pockets dissecting through subcutaneous tissues and extending between adjacent osseous structures.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Septic Arthritis / Gas-Forming Tenosynovitis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The presence of soft-tissue gas on CT, fluctuant warm swelling, marked CRP elevation, and polynuclear leukocyte-rich exudate strongly suggested acute pyogenic or anaerobic bacterial infection; however, exhaustive aerobic and anaerobic cultures on blood agar, chocolate agar, and BHI broth remained sterile after 15 days.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: After 15 days of incubation, all cultures and subcultures returned as sterile.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Complicated Non-Infectious Diabetic / Neuropathic Arthropathy (Charcot Foot)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Although peripheral neuropathy and diabetes predispose to destructive Charcot joint disease, the presence of an extensive purulent fluid collection with deep soft tissue and tendinous infiltration confirmed an active suppurative infectious process.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Soft tissue ultrasound revealed a poorly defined hypoechoic, heterogeneous swelling that extended into the joint, with infiltration of the muscular and tendinous structures. This suggested a complicated abscessed tenosynovitis and myositis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Because of non-improvement and persistent negative pyogenic cultures, repeated joint aspirate was examined for mycobacteria, demonstrating acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining, followed by positive cultures on Lowenstein-Jensen and MGIT media and real-time PCR (GeneXpert MTB/RIF) confirming Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex without rifampicin resistance.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Mycobacterial testing was conducted on the lavage fluid and revealed acid-fast bacilli (AFB) on direct examination (Fig. 1) using the Ziehl-Neelsen staining method

editor_comments: Distilled in strict adherence to Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology. Admission prompt stops prior to surgical joint lavage, microbiological cultures, and mycobacterial testing without disclosing pathogen or diagnosis. Verbatim quotes support all differential reasoning.
